open_points.subject: R0-01 storage boundary versus R0-06 Customer records
open_points.text: “Registry owns project identity, nothing else”; “Registry stores identity and pointers only”; but “Registry holds a Customer record: who the project is for and how to reach them — name, phone, e-mail, language.”
open_points.question: Does “identity” explicitly include Registry-owned Customer contact data, or is the identity-and-pointers-only boundary meant to exclude such data?
options: Identity includes Customer identity and contact data
The storage boundary must be restated with Customer contact data as an explicit exception
Customer contact data must not be stored in Registry
open_points.default_guess: Treat Customer identity and contact data as an explicit part of Registry-owned identity data because R0-06 is the more specific decision.

open_points.subject: R0-05 cross-instance project identity
open_points.text: “Two instances share nothing; the same physical object in two instances is two projects unless the caller gives both the same id” and “One physical object can therefore carry one id across instances.”
open_points.question: When two independent instances contain records with the same caller-supplied project_id, are these still two independent projects that merely share an identifier, or one logical project spanning instances?
options: Two independent records with the same identifier
Cross-instance identity equality has no defined meaning
open_points.default_guess: Treat them as two independent records that share an identifier; there is no synchronization or shared ownership.

open_points.subject: Browser access to an internal-only Registry
open_points.text: “Browser — the Registry frontend from its own origin; CORS admits exactly that origin” but “An instance reachable from beyond its host is a wrong deployment.”
open_points.question: How can a browser outside the Registry host call the Registry API directly, as the CORS promise implies, while the API must never be reachable beyond that host?
options: The browser is used only on the Registry host
An external frontend backend or proxy calls Registry, so the browser does not call it directly
A proxy exposes the Registry API beyond the host
Browsers connect through a private network or VPN that counts as inside
open_points.default_guess: Use a frontend backend or proxy as the internal Registry client and remove the implication that the browser calls Registry directly.

open_points.subject: Extent of the permitted network boundary
open_points.text: “listening only on loopback or on the deployment's internal network” but “An instance reachable from beyond its host is a wrong deployment.”
open_points.question: May Registry be reached from another host on a private deployment network, or must every permitted caller be on the same physical host?
options: Any host on the deployment's private internal network
Only explicitly named hosts on that internal network
open_points.default_guess: Require the same physical host, including its local container network, because the text explicitly rejects reachability beyond the host.

open_points.subject: Credential transport over the internal network
open_points.text: “They reach Registry over HTTP on the host's loopback or the deployment's internal network” and “service tokens and the staff credential” are secrets that are “never in a record, a log line or an answer.”
open_points.question: Is the deployment's internal network trusted to carry credentials over plaintext HTTP, or must credential-bearing requests have transport encryption or another confidential channel?
options: Plaintext HTTP is permitted because the internal network is trusted
TLS is required whenever traffic leaves loopback
A trusted local proxy terminates TLS before forwarding internally
Mutual TLS or an equivalent authenticated channel is required
open_points.default_guess: Require TLS whenever requests leave loopback, while permitting plaintext HTTP on loopback.
